blocks.markdown: **Security transactions: the organizing map.** The syllabus covers pledge, mortgage, real estate mortgage, chattel mortgage, foreclosure and equitable mortgage. Begin every problem by identifying the **principal obligation**, the **collateral**, **who owns and who possesses** the collateral, the **form and registration requirements**, and the **enforcement procedure**. Pledge and mortgage are **accessory contracts**: their purpose is to **secure an obligation, not automatically to transfer ownership** to the creditor.

A secured loan gives the creditor a **security right over property** if the debtor fails to perform. Security does **not** ordinarily allow the creditor to **simply take ownership of the collateral after default**. The creditor must use the **remedy and procedure allowed by law**.
Common requisites of pledge and mortgage: Arts. 2085–2092

The reviewer states the common requisites as follows: (1) the pledge or mortgage is **constituted to secure the fulfillment of a principal obligation**; (2) the pledgor or mortgagor must be the **absolute owner** of the thing given as security, subject to the applicable rules and exceptions; (3) the person constituting the security must have **free disposal** of the property or be **legally authorized** to dispose of it; (4) the secured obligation must be **valid**, although security may secure **future or conditional obligations** as allowed by the Code; (5) the security contract does **not itself vest ownership** of the collateral in the creditor; and (6) the security is **accessory**: generally it **follows the secured obligation** and is extinguished when the obligation is extinguished, subject to the applicable statutory rules.

A pledge or mortgage is generally **indivisible even if the debt or the property is divisible**. The **whole collateral may remain liable for the unpaid portion** until the secured obligation is fully satisfied, subject to statutory exceptions. Do **not** assume that part payment automatically releases a proportional part of the collateral unless the law or agreement provides it.

**Exact elements to recite:** (1) property is **pledged or mortgaged as security for a principal obligation**; and (2) there is a **stipulation allowing the creditor automatically to appropriate the collateral** upon the debtor's failure to pay within the stipulated period. A stipulation of automatic appropriation is **void**. The security contract itself is **not necessarily void in its entirety**.

**Exam use: substance prevails over the label “dacion en pago.”** Ask whether the debtor truly made a **later voluntary transfer independent of the security**, or whether the transfer was **prearranged to vest collateral in the creditor automatically upon default**.

A document called a **sale with right to repurchase** may be treated as a mortgage if the statutory circumstances show it was intended **only as security for a debt**. Art. 1602 lists presumptive circumstances, including **gross inadequacy of price**; the **vendor remaining in possession** as lessee or otherwise; a **repeated or extended redemption period**; the **buyer retaining part of the price**; the **seller paying taxes**; or other circumstances showing the true intention was to secure an obligation. Art. 1603 **resolves doubt in favor of an equitable mortgage**. The label is not conclusive; **intent and circumstances matter**.

blocks.markdown: **Final checklist (general):** pledge and mortgage are **accessory security contracts, not automatic transfers of ownership**; Art. 2088 pactum commissorium requires **security collateral plus automatic appropriation on default**; an equitable mortgage is determined by **statutory presumptions and real intent, not the document label**.
